quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Collective noun stays singular, even with a relative clause containing a plural noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The advisory board that reviews these applications ___ its recommendations by the end of the month.
quests.completedSentence: The advisory board that reviews these applications submits its recommendations by the end of the month.
quests.grammarRule: Collective noun stays singular, even with a relative clause containing a plural noun
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The advisory board' is a singular collective noun; 'applications' inside the relative clause is just a distractor. The verb takes -s: 'submits'.
quests.nativeTip: 'That reviews these applications' describes the board - the true subject is still one singular body.
quests.example: The advisory board that reviews these applications submits its recommendations by the end of the month.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Quantity expression + plural countable noun takes a plural verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: A majority of the committee members who attended the hearing ___ undecided.
quests.completedSentence: A majority of the committee members who attended the hearing remain undecided.
quests.grammarRule: Quantity expression + plural countable noun takes a plural verb
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Committee members' is countable and plural, so 'a majority of the committee members' takes a plural verb: 'remain'.
quests.nativeTip: 'A majority of' agrees with the noun that follows 'of' - check whether that noun is countable and plural.
quests.example: A majority of the committee members who attended the hearing remain undecided.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The panel overseeing these decisions, along with two outside consultants, ___ holding its final session next week.
quests.completedSentence: The panel overseeing these decisions, along with two outside consultants, is holding its final session next week.
quests.grammarRule: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The panel' is a singular collective noun; 'along with two outside consultants' is extra detail. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Ask whether 'along with' adds a second subject or just extra detail.
quests.example: The panel overseeing these decisions, along with two outside consultants, is holding its final session next week.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Each of' + plural noun phrase still takes a singular verb, even with a long descriptive phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Each of the theories proposed by researchers in this field ___ its own limitations.
quests.completedSentence: Each of the theories proposed by researchers in this field has its own limitations.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each of' + plural noun phrase still takes a singular verb, even with a long descriptive phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Each of the theories' is singular; 'proposed by researchers in this field' is just extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'has'.
quests.nativeTip: Which word is the subject: 'each', or something in the description after it?
quests.example: Each of the theories proposed by researchers in this field has its own limitations.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Every' + singular noun takes a singular verb, even with a long descriptive phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Every conclusion drawn from the data collected across multiple trials ___ careful scrutiny.
quests.completedSentence: Every conclusion drawn from the data collected across multiple trials requires careful scrutiny.
quests.grammarRule: 'Every' + singular noun takes a singular verb, even with a long descriptive phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Every conclusion' is singular; the phrase about data and trials is extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'requires'.
quests.nativeTip: Ask what 'every' does to its noun, then set the long description aside.
quests.example: Every conclusion drawn from the data collected across multiple trials requires careful scrutiny.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Neither of' + plural noun phrase still takes a singular verb, even with a long descriptive phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Neither of the models tested in this round of experiments ___ fully accurate.
quests.completedSentence: Neither of the models tested in this round of experiments seems fully accurate.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither of' + plural noun phrase still takes a singular verb, even with a long descriptive phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Neither of the models' is singular; 'tested in this round of experiments' is extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'seems'.
quests.nativeTip: Think about how 'neither of' behaves, whatever description follows.
quests.example: Neither of the models tested in this round of experiments seems fully accurate.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even with an appositive attached to the other noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Either the mayor, a longtime advocate for public transit, or the city council ___ expected to announce its new funding plan.
quests.completedSentence: Either the mayor, a longtime advocate for public transit, or the city council is expected to announce its new funding plan.
quests.grammarRule: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even with an appositive attached to the other noun
quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the city council', a singular collective noun, so the verb is 'is', regardless of the appositive describing the mayor.
quests.nativeTip: With 'either...or', check the noun closest to the verb - the appositive on the first noun doesn't matter.
quests.example: Either the mayor, a longtime advocate for public transit, or the city council is expected to announce its new funding plan.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Not only the residents of the flooded neighborhoods but also the local government ___ demanding immediate action from its state partners.
quests.completedSentence: Not only the residents of the flooded neighborhoods but also the local government is demanding immediate action from its state partners.
quests.grammarRule: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the local government', a singular collective noun, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Apply the same proximity rule here, ignoring the prepositional phrase on the first noun.
quests.example: Not only the residents of the flooded neighborhoods but also the local government is demanding immediate action from its state partners.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even with an embedded phrase attached to the other noun
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Neither the witnesses, several of whom saw the incident, nor the officer ___ certain about the exact time.
quests.completedSentence: Neither the witnesses, several of whom saw the incident, nor the officer is certain about the exact time.
quests.grammarRule: Correlative conjunction agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even with an embedded phrase attached to the other noun
quests.ruleExplanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the officer', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Even with an embedded clause describing the witnesses, the noun closest to the verb still decides the agreement.
quests.example: Neither the witnesses, several of whom saw the incident, nor the officer is certain about the exact time.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject, even with a relative clause inside it

quests.grammarRule: 'Along with' does not change the number of the original subject, even with a relative clause inside it
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The board' is a singular collective noun; 'along with the shareholders who raised concerns last quarter' is extra detail. The verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: The shareholders and their relative clause are extra detail - the true subject is still the singular board.
quests.example: The board, along with the shareholders who raised concerns last quarter, is scheduled to cast its vote on the proposal.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Together with' does not change the number of the original subject, even with a relative clause inside it

quests.nativeTip: Ask whether 'together with' and the clause after it can change the main subject.
quests.example: This policy, together with the amendments that were added last year, remains under review by legal counsel.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Accompanied by' does not change the number of the original subject

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Gerund phrase stays singular, even when it contains a compound object

quests.grammarRule: Gerund phrase stays singular, even when it contains a compound object
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Balancing a full-time job and two young children' is a gerund phrase and is singular. The verb takes -s: 'requires'.
quests.nativeTip: Decide whether this gerund phrase names one activity or two.
quests.example: Balancing a full-time job and two young children requires more energy than she ever expected.

quests.ruleExplanation: 'To manage both the budget and the schedule' is an infinitive phrase and is singular. The verb is 'is'.

quests.example: To manage both the budget and the schedule for this event is no easy task.
